question: Fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size, as in species of Eudorina is termed as ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**anisogamous**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Algae are chlorophyll-bearing organisms, with a simple thalloid-like structure and, are autotrophic in the mode of nutrition.
 
• Algae live primarily aquatic organisms which may live in both freshwater and marine water.
 
• The algae reproduce by vegetative, asexual, and sexual methods.
 
• Sexual reproduction in algae takes place through the fusion of two gametes.
 
• Sexual reproduction is of three types.
 
 
• Isogamous
 
• Anisogamous
 
• Oogamous
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/59d038566d791b05d7ece0dfbd5dcfce81deec2b8d36678a71ef557870c92af4.png] 

 
• Anisogamous is a condition in which fusion of two gametes takes place which is dissimilar in size.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Isogamous is a condition in which the fusion of two gametes takes place which is similar in size.

 
 
• For example - Spirogyra, Ulothrix.
 
 
 
• Oogamous is a condition in which fusion between one large, nonmotile (static) female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete occurs.
 
 
• For example- Volvox.
 
 
 
• In algae, vegetative reproduction occurs through fragmentation
 
 
• Each fragment develops into a thallus.
 
• In Asexual reproduction in algae, different types of spores are produced.
